full_judgment: 15. In the case of Md Insan Ali vs. Mir Abdus Salam 1988 BCR (AD) 125 on the point of service of notice it was observed: "Examination of the process-server is mandatory when he has simply submitted his report about the service of summons without any verification or declaration that he had served the summons, but when he made a declaration to this effect then his examination as a witness is not mandatory, although the court may at its discretion call him as a witness." On reference to the observation in para 6 of the report Mr Huq addressed on us with regard to examination of affidavit, verification, declaration of the process-server and the Officer of the court. In this decision the learned Judge has elaborately discussed the purport of Order 5, rules 17, 19 & 19A. He submits that the aforesaid provision is not mandatory. It has been held in the case of Johara Begum vs. Rafique Kader 25 DLR 91 as under: "From the above provisions it is amply clear that provisions of rule 19 cannot be treated as a dead letter or obsolete. Provisions of Rule 19 are mandatory and same must be complied with due diligence, and court after making necessary inquiry in the matter record a clear findings of due service or otherwise. In the absence of declaration made and subscribed by the process-server, as required under the rules, the service cannot be accepted as evidence of due service. And in the absence of an inquiry made by the court as provided in rule 19 and distinct declaration of due service recorded there is no presumption of service of summons. Presumption of service arises when record shows that process was rightly and duly served." (Emphasis added,) Therefore, in view of the aforesaid observation we hold that the provision is mandatory and not directory. Mr Rafique-ul Huq further contended that there is no wrong in the statement made in the petition for attachment before judgment and the court is to be satisfied from the affidavit or otherwise. He submits that the expression "otherwise" included inability of the appellant to furnish security which was condition precedent for making the order under appeal. Again, it brings the question whether the petitioner was aware of such conditional order. Unless notices of such order is served according to law and service of the order suffers from infirmity or illegality how it can be said that the appellant was unable? Be that as it may, in our opinion the expression "otherwise" does not include "inability to furnish security". Mr Rafique-ul 'Huq cited the decision in the case of Premraj Mundra vs. Md Maneck Gazi and others 1951 (Cal) 156 and argued placing reliance upon para 11 of the report that the court is to consider whether the defence is a bonafide one on the objection to be raised to the petition. In this case such opportunity to the defendant appellant seems to be not available for such sort of inquiry is to be led on valid service of notice. Therefore, the decision of Single Bench of the Calcutta High Court does not apply to the facts of the present case before us. The next decision cited is the case of Abdul Wahab Gazi vs. Sheikh Haider Ali and others; 16 BLD 53 (AD). The Appellate Division at page 54 observed as under: "The learned Judge of the High Court Division upon consideration of the provisions of Rules 17, 19 and 19A of Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure has taken the view, correctly, that the process-server in his report having shown that the summons served upon the pre-emptee by hanging, it was the requirement of law on the part of the trial Court to examine the process-server on oath. The learned Judge further observed correctly that the trial Court mechanically accepted the service report." Mr Rafiqul-ul Huq drew our attention at pages 4, 8 and 9 of the Paper Book and contended that there was declaration. On perusal of the order sheet as contained in the Paper Book we do not find any affidavit. Therefore, the requirement of law has not been fulfilled.
